This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants seeking compensation of Rs. 41,25,000/- as the Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior, vide award dated 22.03.2011 in Claim Case No.109/2009 has dismissed the claim petition of claimants/appellants.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The necessary facts for disposal of this appeal, in brief, are that on 31.05.2009 at around 10:30 pm, deceased along with his friend (respondent No.1) returning home by a Maruti Car bearing Registration No.MP 07 E 6564 which was being driven by respondent No.1 (Ashok Sharma) in a very cautious manner.
Suddenly, a truck came in front of the car, due to which accident occured in which deceased (Tej Singh) received injuries and succumbed on the spot.

Learned counsel for claimants/appellants filed a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicle Act (in short "the Act") and pleaded that deceased used to earn Rs.5,000/- per month, therefore, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.41,25,000/-.
4.
Driver and owner of offending vehicle as well as Insurance Company filed their written statements and denied all the averments.

5. Learned Claims Tribunal framed the issues and after taking evidence, Claims Tribunal has rejected the claim petition on the ground that claimants are not entitled to get the compensation Smt. Preeti Yadav vs Ashok Sharma on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93400332/
1 under Section 163-A of the Act, because the income of the deceased was more than Rs.40,000/- per annum as per IInd Schedule of the Act.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel of appellants that the learned Tribunal has erred in dismissing the claim petition under Section 163-A of the Act on the ground that the claimants themselves have pleaded that income of the deceased was Rs.5,000/- per month and his annual income was Rs.60,000/-.
Therefore, the petition under Section 163-A of the Act is not tenable in as much as the annual income of deceased was more than Rs.40,000/-.

Though, the claimants have pleaded as such, but the Insurance company in its written statement did not plead that as the income of the deceased was more than Rs.40,000/-, the claim petition is not tenable under the provisions of Section 163-A of the Act, hence, no issue has been framed in this regard.

He relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni and others Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd, 2004 ACJ, 934, the judgments of this Court in the case of Deobala & Others Vs. 3 MA-1058-2011 Padwal Janaji & Others, I (2006) ACC 50, Gitesh (Smt.) & Others Vs. Badri Prasad & Another, II (2006)ACC 136 (DB), Usha Rathore and Others Vs. National Insurance Co.Ltd.
and others, 2009 ACJ 214, Munda Tai and Others Vs.New India Assurance Co.Ltd,
MANU/MP/1913/2012 and also a judgment of Guwahati High Court in the case of United India Insurace Co. Ltd Vs. B.L. Rochunga and another, 2009 (2) ACCD 865 (Guwahati).

sentences.text: Hence, keeping in view the death of the deceased, the compensation amount must be awarded to the claimants/appellants and also prayed for dismissal of impugned order of Claims Tribunal.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Insurance Company has opposed the appeal on the ground that the maintainability of petition under provisions of Section 163-A of the Motor the Act is a legal question and on that point, neither any pleadings nor any issue is required.
Since, the claimants/appellants have themselves pleaded that income of the deceased was Rs.5,000/- per month, therefore the annual income is clearly more than Rs.40,000/-.
Under the structured formula under Section 163-A of the Act, the petition is not maintainable before the learned tribunal.
Learned tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition.

He relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni and others Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd, 2004 ACJ, 934 , judgments of this Court in the case of Naseer Khan Vs. 8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

In case of Deobala and Others(supra) the co-ordinate Bench of this Court, in a petition under Section 163-A of the Act has assumed the income of Rs.69,600/- per month awarded the compensation in favour of the claimants.

But, in this case, the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Smt. Preeti Yadav vs Ashok Sharma on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93400332/
2 case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni (supra) has not been considered.

entities.text: Smt. Preeti Yadav vs Ashok Sharma on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similar is the situation in cases of Smt.Gitish (supra) and Munda Tai (supra).
10.

In case of Usha Rathore and others (supra) though a Division Bench of this Court has while considering the law laid down in case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni (supra) , has held that under Section 163-A of the Act, the claim of claimant can be considered in respect of income of deceased upto Rs.40,000/- per annum.

Similar is the law laid down in case of United India Insurance Vs.
B.L.Rochunga (supra) .
However, in this regard, the law laid down in case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni (supra) is pertinent.

Paragraphs 42, 53,56, 66 and 67 of the judgment is relevant and are reproduced as under:-
"42 [ Para 42 corrected vide Corrigendum No. F.3/Ed.B.J./64/2004 dated 12-7-2004] . Section 163-A was, thus, enacted for grant of 5 MA-1058-2011 immediate relief to a section of the people whose annual income is not more than Rs 40,000 having regard to the fact that in terms of Section 163-A of the Act read with the Second Schedule appended thereto, compensation is to be paid on a structured formula not only having regard to the age of the victim and his income but also the other factors relevant therefor.
An award made thereunder, therefore, shall be in full and final settlement of the claim as would appear from the different columns contained in the Second Schedule appended to the Act.
The same is not interim in nature.

The note appended to column 1 which deals with fatal accidents makes the position furthermore clear stating that from the total amount of compensation one-third thereof is to be reduced in consideration of the expenses which the victim would have incurred towards maintaining himself had he been alive.

This together with the other heads of compensation as contained in columns 2 to 6 thereof leaves no manner of doubt that Parliament intended to lay a comprehensive scheme for the purpose of grant of adequate compensation to a section of victims who would require the amount of compensation without fighting any protracted litigation for proving that the accident occurred owing to negligence on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle or any other fault arising out of use of a motor vehicle.

53.Although the Act is a beneficial one and, thus, deserves liberal construction with a view to implementing the legislative intent but it is trite that where such beneficial legislation has a scheme of its own and there is no vagueness or doubt therein, the court would not travel beyond the same and extend the scope of the statute on the pretext of extending the statutory benefit to those who are not covered thereby.
(SeeRegional Director, ESI Corpn.v.Ramanuja Match Industries[(1985) 1 SCC 218 :
1985 SCC (L&S) 213 : AIR 1985 SC 278] .)
56.It is now well settled that for the purpose of interpretation of statute, same is to be read in its entirety.
The purport and object of the Act must be given its full effect.

(SeeHigh Court of Gujaratv.Gujarat Kishan Mazdoor Panchayat(2003) 4 SCC 712 :

Shapoorji Data Processing Ltd(2004) 1 SCC 702 : JT (2003) 9 SC 109 : (2003) 9 Scale 713] and Ashok Leyland Ltd.v.State of T.N.[(2004) 3 SCC 1 : (2004) 1 Scale 224] )

sentences.text: The object underlying the statute is required to be given effect to by applying the principles of purposive construction.

66. We may notice that Section 167 of the Act provides that where death of, or bodily injury to, any person gives rise to claim of compensation under the Act and also under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, he cannot claim compensation under both the Acts.

The Motor Vehicles Act contains different expressions as, for example,
"under the provision of the Act", "provisions of this Act", "under any other provisions of this Act"
or "any other law or otherwise".

In Section 163-A, the expression "notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other 6 MA-1058-2011 law for the time being in force" has been used,
which goes to show that Parliament intended to insert a non obstante clause of wide nature which would mean that the provisions of Section 163- A would apply despite the contrary provisions existing in the said Act or any other law for the time being in force.
Section 163-A of the Act covers cases where even negligence is on the part of the victim.
It is by way of an exception to Section 166 and the concept of social justice has been duly taken care of.
67. We, therefore, are of the opinion that Kodala [(2001) 5 SCC 175 : 2001 SCC (Cri) 857] has correctly been decided.

However, we do not agree with the findings in Kodala[(2001) 5 SCC 175 :
2001 SCC (Cri) 857] that if a person invokes provisions of Section 163-A, the annual income of Rs 40,000 per annum shall be treated as a cap.
In our opinion, the proceeding under Section 163-A being a social security provision, providing for a distinct scheme, only those whose annual income is up to Rs 40,000 can take the benefit thereof.

All other claims are required to be determined in terms of Chapter XII of the Act."
11.

The perusal of the aforesaid paragraphs in case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni (supra),
clearly show that the Section 163-A of the Act was, enacted for grant of immediate relief to a section of people whose annual income is not more than Rs.40,0000/-
having regard to the fact that in terms of Section 163-A of the Act read with Section Second Schedule appended there to; compensation is to be paid on a structured formula not only having regard to the age of victim and his income but also the other relevant factors therefore.

Although, the Act is beneficial one and thus, deserves liberal construction with a view to implementing the legislative intent but it is trite that where such beneficial legislation has a scheme of its own and there is no vagueness or doubt therein, the court would not travel beyond the same and extend the scope of statute on the pretext of extending the statutory benefit to those who are not covered thereby.

In paragraph 67, Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically reaches Smt. Preeti Yadav vs Ashok Sharma on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93400332/
4 to the conclusion that the proceeding under section 163-A of the Act of the Act being a social security provision, providing for a 7 MA-1058-2011 distinct scheme, only those whose annual income is up to Rs.40,000/- can take the benefit thereof.

sentences.text: All other claims are required to be determined in terms of Chapter XII of the Act.

12. The law laid down in case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni (supra) , is very clear on the point if the annual income of the deceased is claimed to be and found to be more than Rs.40,000/- per annum then the claim petition under Section 163-A read with Second Schedule of the Motor Vehicle Act is not maintainable.
Similar law has been laid down in cases of Nasir Khan (supra) and Smt. Prabha and Others (supra) by coordinate Bench of this Court.

13. The view of of this Court as aforesaid has further substantiated by the law laid down in the case of The Branch Manager, Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Dilu Rai and others (supra) and The Branch Manager, The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs. R. Jothi and another(supra).

sentences.text: 14. Here in this case, the claimants in their claim petition have categorically stated in the statement that the claimant/deceased was doing a private job in Ghagoi Food Product Pvt. Ltd and getting per month salary as Rs.5000/-.

Therefore, apparently,
the income of the claimant/deceased was around Rs.60,000/- per annum.

Though,
no stand taken by Insurance Company in reply that looking to the income of the claimant/deceased, the claim petition filed under the provisions of Section 163-A of the Act is not maintainable but being a legal question, the law in this respect can be taken care of.
8 MA-1058-2011 15.

The evidence and argument in respect of enhancement of the compensation amount is redundant in light of the discussion as aforesaid and finding that the claim petition was not maintainable under the provisions of Section 163-A of the Act.
Therefore, the arguments and evidence with regard to the enhancement of the compensation amount are not being considered.

16. The findings of learned claims tribunal in respect of non- maintainability of claim petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicle Act in light of the claim of the claimants in respect of annual income is around Rs.60,000/- does not seem to be erroneous, illegal or perverse and, therefore, does not warrant any interference of this Court.
Being bereft of merit, this appeal is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
